findings.claim: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at inside email validation, and users#create runs validations twice (user.valid? then user.save), so one signup attempt is counted twice and causes extra writes.

verifier.reason: BlockedEmail.should_block? (app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-19) increments match_count, updates last_match_at, and saves the record when called from EmailValidator#validate_each (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13, wired on app/models/user.rb:47). Because UsersController#create calls user.valid? at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 and then unconditionally calls user.save at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:172, validations run twice per signup attempt, incrementing match_count twice and performing two database writes.

findings.claim: pushObject(result.values.email) adds null/undefined to rejectedEmails when the server response omits or blanks values.email.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-276, the guard only checks result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values without checking result.values.email, so pushObject(result.values.email) pushes null, undefined, or an empty string into rejectedEmails when values.email is omitted or blank (which app/controllers/users_controller.rb:199 can return via user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")).

findings.claim: EmailValidator no longer rejects malformed addresses, so validates :email, email: true accepts values like sam@sam or sam.

verifier.reason: EmailValidator#validate_each in lib/validators/email_validator.rb:3-16 only checks domain whitelist/blacklist settings and BlockedEmail.should_block?, without checking email format (such as Email.is_valid? in lib/email.rb:8-15). Consequently, validates :email, email: true in app/models/user.rb:47 accepts malformed values like sam@sam or sam (note that EmailValidator is newly added in this patch and User's prior email_validator also lacked format checks).

findings.claim: The 'last_match_at is null' example tests an ActiveRecord/migration default rather than application logic.

verifier.reason: In spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:12-16, the 'last_match_at is null' example checks that BlockedEmail.create(email: email).last_match_at is nil, but app/models/blocked_email.rb:21-23 only sets action_type in set_defaults and has no creation logic for last_match_at. The nil value comes solely from the nullable column definition t.datetime :last_match_at in db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:7 and ActiveRecord's default behavior.

findings.claim: The modified User model validations have no updated specs.

verifier.reason: The patch modifies User email validations in app/models/user.rb:46-47 to use EmailValidator (which adds blocked-email checking), but spec/models/user_spec.rb (lines 21-22 and 488-566) is completely untouched. The new spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:1-23 only calls EmailValidator#validate_each directly in isolation rather than testing User model validation.
